Summary: The DRAGIN paper by Weihang Su et al. introduces a framework called DRAGIN, which stands for Dynamic Retrieval Augmented Generation based on the Information Needs of Large Language Models. It aims to optimize the process of information retrieval to cater to the LLM's information needs by employing two key frameworks: RIND (Real-time Information Needs Detection) and a method for optimizing multiple retrievals. The paper is accessible via the link provided in the Towards Data Science article. The concept of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) was first introduced in a 2020 paper by Lewis et al., which described combining a parametric language model with an external memory accessed through retrieval at inference time.
